cards.title: Destroy the Patron
cards.explanation: Open a lane through its Guardian, Walker and Base Guardians. Destroy both enemy Shrines, then finish the Patron and its weakened phase.
cards.tip: After winning a fight, help your wave take the next reachable structure.
cards.pitfall: A high kill count does not end the match; the Patron does.

cards.title: Bring your Troopers
cards.explanation: Most structures gain backdoor protection without an enemy Trooper wave nearby. Pushing the wave forward removes that protection.
cards.tip: Clear the enemy wave, then advance with your Troopers before attacking a Walker or the base.
cards.pitfall: Hitting a structure marked Protected can waste your advantage.

cards.title: Walkers unlock more items
cards.explanation: Each enemy Walker your team destroys unlocks one additional inventory slot, up to three. This makes a Walker kill useful for the whole team.
cards.tip: When a safe Walker is exposed, ping it and help finish it.
cards.pitfall: Old guides that tie extra slots to Guardians or Shrines use outdated rules.

cards.title: Collect both halves
cards.explanation: A Trooper's bounty is split between a ground orb and a floating orb. Ground orbs belong to your team; floating orbs can be claimed by either team.
cards.tip: Move close enough to collect your green ground orb, and shoot your floating orb after it lights up.
cards.pitfall: Killing the Trooper alone does not guarantee you collected its entire bounty.

cards.title: Secure yours; deny theirs
cards.explanation: Shooting an enemy's floating orb steals that portion of its reward. A melee last-hit secures the floating portion immediately, avoiding that deny contest.
cards.tip: Use a safe melee finish nearby; still collect the ground orb.
cards.pitfall: Do not walk into enemy damage or an obvious parry just to secure one Trooper.

cards.title: Souls also level you up
cards.explanation: Total souls gathered unlock Boons, abilities and ability upgrades as well as funding your items. Earning steadily gives you more than just shopping money.
cards.tip: Spend newly earned ability points during a safe moment.
cards.pitfall: Do not leave ability unlocks or upgrade points unused through the next fight.

cards.title: Parry the punch
cards.explanation: Every hero can parry melee attacks with F by default. A successful parry stops the hit and stuns the attacker; a missed parry leaves a cooldown.
cards.tip: Practice reacting to a heavy-melee wind-up before queueing.
cards.pitfall: Parry is not a general shield against bullets or most abilities.

cards.title: Keep an escape charge
cards.explanation: Dashes and air jumps consume stamina. A dash-jump uses two stamina in total, so repeated movement inputs can leave you unable to dodge.
cards.tip: Keep one stamina charge when approaching an enemy or a blind corner.
cards.pitfall: Spending every charge to enter a fight can remove your way out.

cards.title: Slide through short routes
cards.explanation: Crouching with enough speed, or downhill, starts a slide. Sliding preserves momentum and lets you fire without consuming ammunition during the slide.
cards.tip: Practice dash, then crouch on a safe lane slope.
cards.pitfall: Crouching while standing still is not a slide.

cards.title: Use the zipline safely
cards.explanation: Look up at your team's line and jump when the connection appears. Recent enemy hero or structure damage blocks attachment, and an exposed rider can be knocked off.
cards.tip: Use cover to leave combat before trying to ride home.
cards.pitfall: Jumping at the line while being shot is not a reliable escape.

cards.title: Turn income into power
cards.explanation: Buy items at a Curiosity Shop to improve damage, survival or utility. Your lane shop closes when its Guardian is destroyed.
cards.tip: Choose a build before the match and shop during a safe break between waves.
cards.pitfall: Do not stand in danger reading item descriptions.

cards.title: Upgrade the component
cards.explanation: An item upgrade consumes its component and discounts the purchase by the component's cost. Selling an item normally refunds only half its cost.
cards.tip: Follow the item's upgrade path instead of selling a component you are about to upgrade.
cards.pitfall: Buying and reselling unrelated items repeatedly wastes souls.

cards.title: Remember active buttons
cards.explanation: Some items provide an ability you must activate; buying them does not use that ability for you.
cards.tip: Check the assigned button when you buy an active item and practice it once safely.
cards.pitfall: A defensive active cannot help if you forget to press it.

cards.title: Check before crossing
cards.explanation: The minimap shows allies and enemies who have been revealed, not the location of every enemy. An absent enemy icon is missing information.
cards.tip: After each wave, check who is visible and choose an exit before entering a district.
cards.pitfall: An empty-looking jungle can still contain an enemy.

cards.title: Wave, nearby farm, wave
cards.explanation: Trooper waves are a dependable income source. Add a nearby box or camp while the next wave travels instead of abandoning several waves for a long detour.
cards.tip: Clear your wave, take one efficient nearby stop, then reassess the lane.
cards.pitfall: A profitable-looking route can lose value if it costs several full waves.

cards.title: Choose a camp you clear quickly
cards.explanation: Triangle markers identify Haunt camps; more lines mean a higher camp tier. A higher-tier camp can contain a mixture of creature sizes.
cards.tip: Start with nearby easier camps and finish every creature before leaving.
cards.pitfall: A large-camp icon does not mean every creature gives the large-creature bounty.

cards.title: Full clears restart the timer
cards.explanation: Camps return after their final creature dies. At mixed Sinner sites, both the machines and the linked Haunts must be cleared.
cards.tip: Clear the whole site when you want it available on a later rotation.
cards.pitfall: Leaving one creature or linked machine alive prevents the normal reset.

cards.title: Break boxes on your path
cards.explanation: Ordinary crates have a chance to drop souls. Large teal Tough Crates require a heavy melee and always drop souls.
cards.tip: Take convenient locked crates and collect the dropped pickup before moving on.
cards.pitfall: A regular crate's reward is an average, not a guaranteed payout.

cards.title: Pick up permanent buffs
cards.explanation: Buff Containers have a 50% chance to drop a permanent stat pickup. New pickups become stronger at 10 and 30 minutes.
cards.tip: Break nearby containers while rotating and collect the booklet they drop.
cards.pitfall: Breaking the container without picking up the booklet gives you no buff.

cards.title: Finish Sinners with timing
cards.explanation: Sinner's Sacrifice machines pay souls when punched and hurt you during the setup hits. A correctly timed heavy-melee jackpot gives four permanent buffs.
cards.tip: Watch the final light pattern, land the heavy jackpot, and check your health before starting another machine.
cards.pitfall: The jackpot can run at different speeds; do not blindly repeat the same timing.

cards.title: Rich spots expose you
cards.explanation: The Bell Tower announces activity with a loud bell; the Sunken Plaza obscures the surroundings and drains stamina. Both can turn a farm stop into an ambush.
cards.tip: Check nearby lanes and enemy positions before entering, and plan how you will leave.
cards.pitfall: A dense cluster of rewards is not automatically a safe farming stop.

cards.title: Protect your recent farm
cards.explanation: Souls from camps, crates and Sinners are haunted until they secure over time. Dying can drop that unsecured portion for another player to claim.
cards.tip: After a large farm run, take a safe route toward your team or your next purchase.
cards.pitfall: A full bag is a reason to avoid a low-odds chase.

cards.title: Escort the Soul Urn
cards.explanation: From 10 minutes, the Urn appears beside a side-lane bridge for delivery to the opposite side. Its carrier cannot use ziplines or teleporters.
cards.tip: Check the destination and ask for cover before picking it up.
cards.pitfall: Do not start a delivery without considering the enemy's route to the drop-off.

cards.title: Contest the Rift together
cards.explanation: An Unstable Rift is a bridge capture objective that awards team souls and a powerful Trooper push. An enemy inside the zone prevents your team from finishing the capture.
cards.tip: Use its announcement to move with teammates and take useful cover near the bridge.
cards.pitfall: More teammates in the circle do not make its base capture progress faster.

cards.title: Claim the crystals after Midboss
cards.explanation: Midboss now drops three separate Rejuvenator crystals. Heavy-melee each landed crystal to claim a shared team revive credit.
cards.tip: Plan to control the pit after the kill, not just damage the boss.
cards.pitfall: The enemy can claim crystals; three credits are shared by the team, not three revives for every player.

cards.title: Check a nearby bridge buff
cards.explanation: Temporary Powerups appear on the bridges from 5 minutes and then at five-minute intervals. Claim one with a heavy melee.
cards.tip: Check a nearby buff when rotating with enough health and an exit route.
cards.pitfall: A bridge is exposed; do not contest alone just because the buff is available.

cards.title: Heal along your route
cards.explanation: Healing Snacks restore health when collected. The October 30 patch increased their healing to 14% of maximum health.
cards.tip: Pick up a nearby snack before a camp or planned fight.
cards.pitfall: Do not use an older guide's 10% healing figure for this patch.

matchStages.title: Opening lanes
matchStages.goal: Collect waves, avoid unnecessary damage, and learn the nearest cover and shop.
actions: Secure floating orbs and collect ground orbs.
Use a safe break to purchase an early item.
Add a small camp only when it does not cost your lane wave.
matchStages.pitfall: Leaving lane for a long farm route before you can clear it efficiently.

matchStages.title: Short rotations
matchStages.goal: Connect lane waves with short, safe trips into the nearby district.
actions: Check medium camps and the nearby bridge Powerup.
From 8:00, consider Sinners or a large camp your build can clear efficiently.
Return toward the next wave or help take an exposed Guardian.
matchStages.pitfall: Starting a hard camp simply because it has spawned.

matchStages.title: Play around objectives
matchStages.goal: Spend your farm and join useful fights around Walkers, Urn routes and Rift announcements.
actions: Push a wave before leaving a lane.
Check missing enemies before a rich farm stop.
Use a won fight to gain a structure or safe map control.
matchStages.pitfall: Continuing a farming loop while your team contests an important nearby objective.

matchStages.title: Convert a lead
matchStages.goal: Keep lanes pushed and move with your team to take base objectives.
actions: Advance behind Troopers to remove protection.
Finish both Shrines and the Patron's two phases when the opening is safe.
matchStages.pitfall: Chasing one retreating enemy while the team could take an objective.

starterHeroes.title: Four ways to learn
starterHeroes.framing: Recommendations for learning styles, not a current power ranking. Pick one or two to repeat while you learn the map.

heroes.name: Infernus
heroes.why: Repeated weapon hits build Afterburn, giving a clear reward for tracking a target. Flame Dash adds a straightforward movement tool.
heroes.firstHabit: Use cover while building the burn; keep a route out.
heroes.watchOut: Running forward to chase every burning enemy can leave you isolated.

heroes.name: Seven
heroes.why: Lightning Ball damages groups, making waves and camps easy to understand. His abilities teach you to punish enemies who stay close together.
heroes.firstHabit: Line up several targets before using your area damage.
heroes.watchOut: Storm Cloud needs line of sight; enemies behind cover are not taking its damage.

heroes.name: Abrams
heroes.why: His close-range weapon, life drain and passive recovery make the brawler role easy to read. He is a useful way to learn cover, melee timing and parries.
heroes.firstHabit: Choose a nearby target your teammates can help you fight.
heroes.watchOut: Durability does not make a predictable heavy punch safe from parry.

heroes.name: Wraith
heroes.why: Full Auto rewards clear shooting windows, and Project Mind offers a targeted teleport. Her kit gives a natural reason to think about an escape position.
heroes.firstHabit: Identify your teleport destination before committing to a fight.
heroes.watchOut: The teleport has an interruptible channel; use it before you are already trapped.

patchHighlights.text: Camps give 10% more base souls and growth, but also have 10% more health and damage.
Box reward growth is 10% lower. The reduction affects growth, not the entire payout.
Haunted souls secure more slowly at baseline; behind players can receive faster securing and stronger comeback rewards.
Midboss now drops three separate Rejuvenator crystals after 7.5 seconds. One heavy melee claims each crystal.
Steam vents now accelerate stamina recovery. Tunnel movement bonus fell from +70% to +50%.

resourceCards.title: Regular boxes
resourceCards.body: Break them while moving. Each has a 60% chance to pay souls; an empty box is normal.
resourceCards.action: Collect the drop and continue toward your next useful stop.

resourceCards.title: Locked boxes
resourceCards.body: The large teal crates need a charged heavy melee. They always pay souls.
resourceCards.action: Take nearby ones when safe; the atlas calls these Locked boxes.

resourceCards.title: Buff containers
resourceCards.body: These have a 50% chance to drop a permanent stat pickup, not spendable souls. Later drops improve at 10:00 and 30:00.
resourceCards.action: Break convenient containers and pick up the reward.

resourceCards.title: Camps / Haunts
resourceCards.body: The triangle's zero, one or two bars mark small, medium or large camps. A larger camp may contain mixed unit sizes.
resourceCards.action: Shoot their eyes, gather nearby monsters for area damage, and finish the whole camp.

resourceCards.title: Sinner's Sacrifice
resourceCards.body: Use four heavy melees, then time a final heavy hit when all bulbs light. A successful heavy jackpot gives four permanent buffs.
resourceCards.action: Budget 320 damage per machine before recovery or mitigation, plus health to escape. Skip it when low.

resourceCards.title: Bridge powerups
resourceCards.body: Glowing stones on the side-lane bridges give a temporary combat or movement buff. Heavy melee claims one.
resourceCards.action: Take a safe nearby buff before rotating; do not cross danger just because it spawned.

resourceCards.title: Soul Urn
resourceCards.body: Melee the landed urn, then carry it to the opposite side. You cannot use ziplines or teleporters, and stuns or melee hits force a drop.
resourceCards.action: Run it when allies can cover the crossing and destination. Shoot the reward orbs to secure them.

resourceCards.title: Midboss
resourceCards.body: Already alive at match start. The kill is followed by three falling crystals; either team can claim them.
resourceCards.action: Go with ready teammates after winning space. Guard the pit until the crystals land and are secured.

resourceCards.title: Unstable Rift
resourceCards.body: A side-lane capture objective with variable timing. Your team must control the circle to claim its team reward.
resourceCards.action: Prepare with teammates when it is announced. Do not treat its timer as an order to enter alone.

resourceCards.title: Spend for the next fight
resourceCards.body: Lane shops close when their Guardian falls. Base shops remain available, and either team can use the secret shops.
resourceCards.action: Buy an affordable useful upgrade after a safe wave, then return to play.

timers.title: Midboss
timers.note: Use the topbar or minimap timer. Availability does not mean your team is ready to kill it.

timers.note: Those times describe the first visual preview. Follow the live announcement for the capture opening.

timingExceptions.text: Not every triangle uses its generic tier timer. The authored map has special early camps at Bodega upstairs, Theater upstairs NE, and Plaza rink 01: 2:00 first spawn and 5:00 return.
A timer starts after the relevant camp is fully cleared. Empty map markers describe locations, not live loot availability.
Sandbox and Explore NYC spawn settings differ from ordinary matches.

priorities.trigger: A nearby wave threatens your tower, or your escape is closing.
priorities.action: Collect the safe wave or retreat first. Leave the farming route unfinished.
priorities.reason: Keeping space and staying alive preserve the next opportunities.

priorities.action: Collect it before taking a long detour. Confirm floating souls and collect ground souls.
priorities.reason: A 15:00 solo four-trooper wave is about 520 souls when fully collected.

priorities.trigger: You can afford a useful next item and have a safe shop window.
priorities.action: Buy after the wave, then return. Do not delay every purchase until the entire route is complete.
priorities.reason: The upgrade can improve both survival and the next camp clear.

priorities.trigger: The wave is handled and enemies are accounted for.
priorities.action: Clear the nearest camp you can finish quickly, collecting boxes and buffs along the way.
priorities.reason: A short useful detour is easier to abandon when the map changes.

priorities.trigger: A large camp is slow or costs too much health.
priorities.action: Skip it; take a closer medium camp or nearby breakables.
priorities.reason: More souls per camp can still mean fewer souls per minute.

priorities.trigger: A Sinner is available and you have health plus an exit.
priorities.action: Clear nearby monsters first. Finish the jackpot with heavy melee; leave if an enemy approaches.
priorities.reason: Retaliation damage makes a long exposed stop vulnerable.

priorities.trigger: Several enemies disappear from nearby lanes.
priorities.action: Move toward your team or a safe lane. Avoid committing to the Tower or deep tunnels.
priorities.reason: Bell Tower loot announces itself, and a farm haul can be lost on death.

priorities.trigger: Your team has numbers, health and nearby waves pushed for an objective.
priorities.action: Finish only the quick safe pickup, then join. After Midboss dies, stay for the crystals.
priorities.reason: The farming loop supports the next useful team action.

priorities.action: Read its local timer and move to an available wave or resource. Return later.
priorities.reason: Respawns are offset by previous clears; there is no endlessly stocked loop.

safetyCards.title: Protect your haul
safetyCards.body: Camp, crate and Sinner souls remain vulnerable until secured over time. A death can drop them. Shopping spends secured souls first, so one purchase may leave haunted souls at risk.

safetyCards.title: Know the exit
safetyCards.body: Bell Tower loot rings a map-wide bell. Sunken Plaza's fog drains stamina. Choose an exit before starting a long clear.

safetyCards.title: Recover before another camp
safetyCards.body: Steam vents hide you from enemy vision and boost regeneration; an enemy entering the vent can reveal you. They are a recovery option, not invulnerability.

safetyCards.title: Step out of telegraphs
safetyCards.body: Move away from monster floor attacks. The updated book monster channels its sleep aura; killing that monster stops the aura.

guardian.label: Lane Guardian
guardian.beginnerExplanation: The first defensive structure in a lane. Push your troopers forward and destroy it to open the way toward the Walker. Its nearby lane shop closes when it falls.

walker.label: Walker
walker.beginnerExplanation: The large defensive structure farther back in each lane. After its Guardian falls, taking the Walker opens the route toward the enemy base.

baseGuardian.label: Base Guardian
baseGuardian.beginnerExplanation: One of a pair guarding a base entrance. Destroy an entire pair to make the enemy Shrines vulnerable.

shrine.label: Shrine
shrine.beginnerExplanation: One of two protected structures inside a base. Destroy both enemy Shrines before attacking the Patron. A Base Guardian pair must fall first.

patron.label: Patron
patron.beginnerExplanation: Your team’s final objective. Defeat the enemy Patron through both phases to win; defend your own. Both protecting Shrines must be destroyed first.

baseTurret.label: Spawn-room turret
baseTurret.beginnerExplanation: An indestructible turret protecting the spawn area. Enemy players approaching the spawn room can be fired upon.

laneShop.label: Lane shop
laneShop.beginnerExplanation: Spend souls on items here while your team’s nearby Guardian survives. Enemy teams cannot use your lane shop.

secretShop.label: Secret shop
secretShop.beginnerExplanation: A neutral underground shop that either team can use. A useful place to buy items during a rotation.

midBoss.label: Mid Boss
midBoss.beginnerExplanation: A powerful neutral boss under Broadway at the center of the map. Usually a team objective: defeating it creates an opportunity to claim Rejuvenator crystals.

timing.note: Respawn follows each defeat; subsequent respawns remain at five minutes.

urnSite.label: Soul Urn location
urnSite.beginnerExplanation: The urn first appears on Yellow at 10:00, then alternates sides every five minutes. Melee to pick it up and carry it across the map. You cannot use ziplines or teleporters while carrying it.

timing.note: An active carried urn can delay the next spawn.

rift.label: Unstable Rift site
rift.beginnerExplanation: A possible site for a capture event. When the Rift opens, stand in its area and clear enemies out to claim team souls and stronger troopers. Only the active event matters.

timing.note: Variable event timing; check the live game announcement.

bridgeBuff.label: Bridge powerup
bridgeBuff.beginnerExplanation: A temporary combat or movement boost. Heavy melee the glowing stone to claim it. Powerups appear from 5:00 on five-minute intervals.

teleporter.label: Teleporter
teleporter.beginnerExplanation: A booth linking distant parts of the map. Enter and channel for four seconds; the selected marker can show its destination. Available from match start.

jumpPad.label: Jump pad
jumpPad.beginnerExplanation: Step onto the pad to launch toward its landing point. You can steer while airborne. Its launch direction is fixed, so inspect the destination before using it.

rope.label: Climb rope
rope.beginnerExplanation: Use the jump input near an orange rope to grab it and move between floors or reach rooftops. Its map point marks the rope, not a walkable doorway.

steamVent.label: Steam vent
steamVent.beginnerExplanation: Standing in the steam hides you from enemies and grants regeneration. Attacking an enemy or an enemy entering the vent can reveal you.

cosmicVeil.label: Cosmic veil
cosmicVeil.beginnerExplanation: A visual barrier you can walk through. It obscures enemies from one side and is useful for escaping or setting up an ambush.

smallCamp.label: Small Haunt camp
smallCamp.beginnerExplanation: A group of weak neutral creatures. Clear it between lane waves when you can return in time. Finish every creature to restart the camp’s respawn timer.

mediumCamp.label: Medium Haunt camp
mediumCamp.beginnerExplanation: A neutral camp with stronger creatures. Group them for an area attack, and check the actual creature mix before committing. Finish the whole camp to restart its timer.

largeCamp.label: Large Haunt camp
largeCamp.beginnerExplanation: A camp containing at least one large neutral creature. The icon does not mean every creature is large. Clear speed depends on your hero and items.

sinner.label: Sinner’s Sacrifice site
sinner.beginnerExplanation: Melee a machine for souls. Time a heavy-melee jackpot for four permanent buffs. Some sites contain several machines or linked Haunts that must all be cleared to restart the respawn timer.

crate.label: Normal crate
crate.beginnerExplanation: Break it while moving between useful stops. It has a chance to drop souls, so a route’s expected crate value is an average rather than a guaranteed payout.

tough.label: Tough crate
tough.beginnerExplanation: Use a heavy melee to open this reinforced crate. It always drops souls. Take it when it fits naturally into your route.

buffContainer.label: Buff container
buffContainer.beginnerExplanation: Break it for a chance at a permanent stat bonus. These bonuses add up over a match and are separate from spendable souls.

healingSnack.label: Healing snack
healingSnack.beginnerExplanation: A small map pickup that restores health over a short time. Check nearby snacks while rotating or recovering after a camp.

guides.title: How to win
guides.body: Push a lane through its Guardian, Walker and Base Guardian pair. Destroy both enemy Shrines, then defeat the Patron through its phases.

guides.title: Know your base
guides.body: Each team has a Patron and two Shrines. The spawn room restores your health and has a shop. Spawn-room turrets punish enemies who chase too far.

guides.title: Where to buy
guides.body: Use your team’s three lane shops while their Guardians survive, either neutral secret shop, or your spawn-room shop.

guides.title: Travel and escape
guides.body: Ziplines follow the lanes. Teleporters connect distant areas; jump pads and ropes change your route or elevation. Steam vents provide concealment. Hero-only tunnel entrances are not interchangeable with steam vents.

guides.title: Read a camp
guides.body: Small, medium and large icons describe the highest tier in a camp, not every creature. Finish linked creatures and machines to restart its timer.

guides.title: Farm a Sinner
guides.body: Melee for souls, then time a heavy-melee jackpot for four permanent buffs. One map marker can contain several machines.

guides.title: Crates and permanent buffs
guides.body: Normal crates have a chance to drop souls. Tough crates require heavy melee and always drop souls. Buff containers may grant permanent stats.

guides.title: Useful pickups
guides.body: Healing snacks help you recover; bridge powerups give a temporary combat or movement bonus.

guides.title: Run the Soul Urn
guides.body: It first appears on Yellow at 10:00 and then alternates sides. Melee to pick it up, carry it to the other side, and secure its reward orbs. Ziplines and teleporters cannot be used while carrying.

guides.title: Neutral objectives
guides.body: Mid Boss is underground at the center. An Unstable Rift is a capture event on a side-lane bridge. Coordinate with your team before leaving a lane for either.

notPinned.reason: Both bases have a shop, but exact paired doorway coordinates are not established. Included in base-zone guidance instead.

notPinned.feature: Distinct Urn pickup and delivery pads
notPinned.reason: The current retrieved layer exposes two generic Soul Urn location markers without separate roles. Do not invent extra precise pads from old six-spawn datasets.

Only geographic names and derived label anchors are provided; no surveyed polygons.

newSourceLootDifferences.note: Compy’s live loot counts differ from the established Atlas snapshot. This proposal preserves existing farm/loot positions rather than silently replacing the prior counted routes.
